mechanism_narrative: GDP growth, as measured by GDPC1, indicates a strong economy which drives corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO exceeds 105 but S&P 500 returns do not exceed 2% over the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) rises and employment (PAYEMS) falls, it signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) stimulate economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is below 0.5 but the Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate consumer demand strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If HOUST and RSAFS are positive but S&P 500 returns do not exceed 3% over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS grows but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) but falling GDP (GDPC1) indicates supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises and GDPC1 falls but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE) indicate tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls but S&P 500 returns are positive when triggered.
